text:
Jake Neighbours is 24, an alternate captain, and a forward who plays heavy: 61 hits in 20 games to go with 9 points, 4 of them on the power play. The Bleedin' Blue headline from Nov. 10 sums up where he is: "Jake Neighbours brings the energy, and now the Blues need the goals."

The worry is at 5-on-5. St. Louis has taken only 42.3% of expected goals with him on the ice, a measure of who is getting the better chances, and that is 9.2 points worse than the team does without him. His points have actually been propped up a little: the Blues have scored 7.3 more goals than those chances deserve while he plays. His own finishing is level, 4 goals on 3.98 expected.

Last season was the high-water mark. Evolving-Hockey had him worth 2.4 wins above replacement, 34th among 401 forwards, with strong defensive impact, but also warned that his results ran ahead of his chances (2.4 wins against 0.7 expected). This year looks like that warning coming true. With 1 goal in his last ten games, we'd watch whether his line starts winning its shifts again before the scoring returns.
headline: Neighbours brings the hits; the Blues need the goals
